national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu said that today national security extends beyond military capabilities and it requires close cooperation between scientific institutions and the armed forces to translate innovation into practical solutions. She said this during interaction with the faculty and course members of the 66th National Defence College Course at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the security and technological landscapes are changing rapidly, bringing new and complex challenges. President Murmu noted that these developments call for greater preparedness, strategic foresight and the ability to adapt to changing circumstances. She added that the fast decision-making mechanism is also becoming more important because the techniques of modern warfare have expanded into cyber security, space technology, and biotechnology apart from the traditional domains. Further, President Murmu said that recent conflicts have highlighted the importance of cost-effective technologies that complement advanced defence systems and make the best use of available resources. She also underlined the importance of government initiatives such as the Research, Development and Innovation Scheme, for strengthening the link between innovation and national security. The President said that the use of Artificial Intelligence in various domains of science, national security and economic activities is increasing. She said that decision making cannot be outsourced exclusively to this technology and emphasised the need for a balanced approach. The President also underlined that economic resilience is an integral part of the national security framework. She said that the Indian economy has demonstrated its capabilities to absorb disruptions created by external factors. The President highlighted that India has accomplished this without compromising the strategic freedom of action.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 165 PM Modi says digital power has opened up greater opportunities for India; Addresses Bloomberg New...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Centre has embodied the principle of Power to Empower in its governance approach and work culture. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Mr Modi said that India’s progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities. He said that power is not just the ability to move ahead, but it is also the ability to empower others. He said that in the present era, digital power has emerged as one of the key drivers of this transformation and is playing a significant role in advancing this vision. Mr Modi stated that digital power has opened up greater opportunities for India. Prime Minister Modi said that India’s economic growth is taking place on a strong foundation amidst global uncertainty. He said the GDP growth stood at 7.8% in the first quarter of this financial year. Mr Modi highlighted that today, India’s foreign exchange reserves exceed 700 billion dollars and the banking system is in its strongest position in many decades. Prime Minister said India’s reform express continues to move ahead at high speed. Prime Minister said that India’s progress in the twenty-first century is a story of advancing together with everyone and carrying everyone along. He said, whenever the world needs a steady pillar, India extends its hand in support, recognizing its responsibility. Mr Modi said today, India is home to more than two thousand Global Capability Centres that are providing services to companies across the world. Prime Minister said technology, data, knowledge and innovation have become important sources of power in the twenty-first century. He said, the government constant endeavour is to ensure that India’s capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well. Mr Modi said, India is the Mother of Democracy, and it has over 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels.’ Mr Modi highlighted that India had lifted twenty-five crore people out of poverty over the past decade. Prime Minister Modi said India’s startup ecosystem has expanded significantly since 2014, with the number of startups crossing 2,50,000. He noted that nearly half of these startups come from smaller cities and towns, while more than 45% have at least one woman director or partner.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 282 HM Amit Shah hails BIMSTEC as important platform for regional integration, economic cooperation a...
national_raw_news.content: India is hosting the first Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi. This historic meeting highlights the collective commitment to combating terrorism, transnational organized crime, narcotics, radicalization, human trafficking, illicit financial flows, and cyber threats. Speaking on the occasion, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that BIMSTEC has emerged as an important platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. He said India has always been committed to peace and human welfare, guided by the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. Mr Shah reiterated that India respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries and believes in the peaceful resolution of disputes. Reaffirming India’s policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, the Union Home Minister called for a collective commitment to ensure that no terrorist network finds space within the region for shelter, recruitment, training, financing or activities against neighbouring countries. Mr Shah also emphasised mutual assistance in extradition and legal cooperation, in accordance with national laws and applicable treaties. He said criminal networks operate across borders and exploit local vulnerabilities. Mr Shah stressed the need for real-time cooperation and coordination among intelligence, law enforcement, financial monitoring and border management agencies. On counter-terrorism cooperation, the Minister stressed the exchange of actionable intelligence through designated nodal agencies and better coordination against terrorist financing and organised crime. Mr Shah said India has achieved significant success in bringing fugitive criminals back from different parts of the world to face justice. He appealed to all BIMSTEC members to strengthen cooperation to ensure that no criminal or terrorist can evade the law, regardless of where they are hiding. BIMSTEC is a regional organisation established in 1997 to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries around the Bay of Bengal and its neighbourhood. It has seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. It aims to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal and in its neighbourhood.

national_raw_news.title: Shefali Verma, Shubman Gill named ICC Women’s and Men’s Player of Month for September 2026 3 hours ago 85
national_raw_news.content: Indian opener Shafali Verma was named the ‘ICC Women’s Player of the Month’ winner for September 2026, following incredible title-winning outings in the Women’s Asia Cup and the Asian Games with the bat and clutch contributions in high-stakes matches. On the other hand, Indian captain Shubman Gill was named ICC men’s Player of the Month for a record fifth time following his outstanding performance in the One Day International series against the West Indies. It is the second time Shafali has won the monthly award, with the 22-year-old first tasting success in November last year when she helped India claim the ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup on home soil, as per the ICC. Shafali Verma, was the highest run-scorer for her team as India won the Women’s Asia Cup. Shubman Gill, as per the ICC, won the award ahead of fellow nominees Abhishek Sharma of India and Zimbabwe’s Sikandar Raza. Gill scored 333 runs in India’s first two One Day Internationals against West Indies, with a century in the opener and an unbeaten double century in the second. India won both matches by eight wickets. This is Gill’s fifth ICC Men’s Player of the Month award, after wins in January 2023, September 2023, February 2025 and July 2025, extending his record as the men’s player with the most wins.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Coast Guard inducts indigenous ALH MK-III Helicopter in Maharashtra 3 hours ago 53
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Coast Guard inducted indigenous Advanced Light Helicopter (ALH MK-III) aircraft, CG 875, into the Coast Guard Region (West) at Ratnagiri in Maharashtra today. The aircraft was received at Coast Guard Air Station, Ratnagiri, with a traditional ‘water cannon salute’. The Commanding Officer, ICGAS Ratnagiri, welcomed the aircraft and crew. The induction of ALH MK-III at Ratnagiri marks a significant enhancement in the operational capability of the Indian Coast Guard along the West Coast. The state-of-the-art helicopter is equipped with Advanced Radar, integrated with long-range imaging and identification capabilities through its Electro Optical Pod and Automatic Identification System. The aircraft is additionally equipped for target neutralisation with its cabin mounted 12.7 mm Heavy Machine Gun. These enhanced surveillance, detection, identification and response capabilities will significantly augment the ICG ability to safeguard nation’s maritime interests within the EEZ, especially along the sensitive coast of Maharashtra The induction of CG 875 is particularly significant as it is the first of the allotted five ALH MK-III aircraft to be positioned with 831 Sqn (CG) at Ratnagiri. The progressive induction of the remaining aircraft will substantially augment the Squadron’s operational capability and enable sustained aerial surveillance and response over the vast maritime area of Coast Guard Region (West), which faces diverse challenges owing to its strategic importance and geographical location.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, CM Rekha Gupta launch 5 EV charging stations, inaugurate 13 Air Quality Monitoring Stations 3 hours ago 78
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Environment and Forests Bhupender Yadav, along with Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, launched five public EV charging stations and inaugurated 13 new Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations in New Delhi today. Talking to the media, Mr Yadav praised Ms Gupta’s leadership in implementing measures to address air pollution in Delhi, saying that the government had taken steps to put 11 action points into practice at a major pollution hotspot. Highlighting the reported improvement in air quality at the hotspot, Mr Yadav said the Air Quality Index (AQI), which stood at 430 on 30th August, had declined to 92 today. He said that the Delhi government increased the combined fleet of electric and CNG buses to over five thousand 500 in line with the commitment earlier made to the CAQM. The Union Minister added that the government had established charging infrastructure and coordinated the efforts of the Delhi Traffic Police, Public Works Department and other agencies to address pollution. Speaking on the occasion, the Delhi Chief Minister said that the Delhi government is strengthening its fight against pollution through real-time monitoring of air quality. She said that this initiative marks a significant step towards real-time monitoring of the Air Quality Index from every corner of the national capital.
